brief: Morgan Stanley's weekly sales note argues markets enter 4Q on a razor's edge: a strong first three quarters is colliding with rising risk malaise from rates, oil and credit, even as the underlying earnings story stays intact. Yields sit at multi-decade highs, making the 10Y a hurdle rate, while headline index strength masks narrow breadth (just 23% of S&P 500 names above their 50-day average, 54%+ of Russell 3000 names in a 20%+ drawdown). September payrolls (29K) and a downward PCE revision eased near-term Fed-hike pressure, but Morgan Stanley's economist still forecasts 50bp more tightening via December and March hikes, with a hot CPI print able to put October back in play. In Europe, France's fiscal-watchdog warning on its 2027 budget drove the sharpest one-day OAT spread move since 2020 (widest since 2012), spilling into Italy on positioning rather than fundamentals. Hedge funds stayed net sellers of equities, trimming Energy and Health Care, with leverage mixed across regions. The conclusion: if yields and oil stay elevated, a strong Q3 earnings season (consensus +26% YoY EPS) is the catalyst that could restore confidence before conditions turn colder.
